title: Switch to LED Bulbs
description: Replace traditional incandescent bulbs with LED alternatives. LEDs use up to 75% less energy and last 25 times longer, significantly reducing your electricity bill and carbon footprint.

title: Unplug Idle Electronics
description: Devices on standby still consume 'phantom power'. Unplugging chargers, TVs, and appliances when not in use can reduce your home energy use by up to 10%.

title: Use Smart Power Strips
description: Smart power strips automatically cut power to devices in standby mode, preventing phantom energy drain across multiple connected electronics simultaneously.

title: Set Your Thermostat Wisely
description: Lowering your heating by just 1°C can cut your heating bill by up to 10%. Use a programmable thermostat to automatically adjust temperatures when you sleep or leave home.

title: Fix Leaky Taps Immediately
description: A dripping tap can waste over 15 litres of water per day. Fixing leaks promptly is one of the simplest and most impactful water conservation actions you can take.

title: Take Shorter Showers
description: Reducing your shower time from 10 to 5 minutes can save up to 40 litres of water per shower. Consider using a timer to keep track of your shower duration.

title: Collect Rainwater for Plants
description: Install a rain barrel under a downspout to collect rainwater. This free, chemical-free water is ideal for watering your garden and reduces demand on municipal water supplies.

title: Run Full Loads Only
description: Run your dishwasher and washing machine only when fully loaded. This maximises efficiency and can save thousands of litres of water over the course of a year.

title: Rinse Before Recycling
description: Food contamination is the leading cause of recyclables being rejected. Give containers a quick rinse to ensure your paper, plastic, and metal items are accepted at recycling facilities.

title: Know Your Plastic Codes
description: Not all plastics are recyclable curbside. Look for the recycling triangle with numbers 1 (PET) and 2 (HDPE) — these are most widely accepted. Avoid codes 3, 6, and 7 when possible.

title: Compost Food Waste
description: Up to 30% of household waste is organic matter that could be composted. Composting reduces landfill methane emissions and creates rich, free fertiliser for your garden.

title: E-Waste Drop-Off Points
description: Old phones, laptops, and batteries contain toxic materials that harm ecosystems if landfilled. Find your nearest certified e-waste drop-off point for safe, responsible disposal.

title: Bring Reusable Bags
description: A single reusable bag replaces hundreds of single-use plastic bags over its lifetime. Keep one folded in your pocket or car so you're always prepared at checkout.

title: Buy Local & Seasonal Produce
description: Food transported long distances contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions. Choosing local and seasonal produce supports farmers in your community and dramatically cuts food miles.

title: Choose Products With Less Packaging
description: Before buying, consider the amount of packaging involved. Choose items with minimal, recyclable, or compostable packaging. Buying in bulk is often the most packaging-efficient option.

title: Support Certified Eco Brands
description: Look for certifications like Fair Trade, B Corp, Rainforest Alliance, or organic labels when shopping. These marks guarantee the product meets verified social and environmental standards.
